# Canonical Data Model — First-Touch Ad Attribution

> **Scope**: how a conversation is tied to the ad that produced it, and how revenue is traced back along that path.
> **Issue**: [#113](https://github.com/Freshair129/zuri1.0/issues/113) Phase 4.
> **Companion**: [`crm-customer-360.md`](./crm-customer-360.md) · [`crm-attribution-invariants.sql`](./crm-attribution-invariants.sql)

## Status — this model is specified, not implemented

Phase 4 of #113 asks to "decide whether `firstTouchAdId` references internal `Ad.id` or Meta
`adId`, then enforce one representation." Auditing the code first turned up something that
changes the shape of that task:

**Nothing writes `firstTouchAdId`. Anywhere.** All four references to it in `src/` are reads,
and two of those are broken. The field has been in the schema, in the PRD, in the ERD, and in
the ROAS formula since Phase 26 — and no code path has ever populated it.

So there is no existing representation to standardise on. This document specifies the model
*before* the writer is built, which is the only remaining moment where choosing costs nothing.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Decided here** | the key representation (§2), the write-path contract (§4), the invariants (§6) |
| **Deliberately not done** | no `@relation` added, no schema change, no application code touched |
| **Why no code** | the three broken reads in §5 are being repaired in a separate task; and the writer in §4 is a feature, not a migration |

---

## 1. The chain

```
Conversation.firstTouchAdId
      │
      │  (logical — no FK, see §3)
      ▼
    Ad.adId ──► AdSet.adSetId ──► Campaign.campaignId ──► AdAccount.accountId
                                                                    │
                                                                    ▼
                                                            AdAccount.tenantId
```

Every enforced hop in that chain joins on a **Meta business key**, never on the internal
`id` column:

| Relation | Declared as | Joins on |
|---|---|---|
| `Ad → AdSet` | `@relation(fields: [adSetId], references: [adSetId])` | Meta `adset_id` |
| `AdSet → Campaign` | `@relation(fields: [campaignId], references: [campaignId])` | Meta `campaign_id` |
| `Campaign → AdAccount` | `@relation(fields: [adAccountId], references: [accountId])` | Meta `account_id` |

`Ad.adId` is `@unique`, so it is a valid target for a reference.

### 1.1 Tenant lives only at the far end

`Ad`, `AdSet` and `Campaign` have **no `tenantId` column**. Only `AdAccount` does. Tenant is
therefore recoverable only by walking the whole chain — and `Ad.adSetId` is **nullable**, so an
ad with no ad-set has no path to a tenant at all.

`marketingRepo.js` already does this correctly. Every ad query in it scopes through
`ac.tenant_id` on the joined `ad_accounts` row rather than filtering ads directly — verified
across all 12 query functions. That is the right pattern and must be preserved: **there is no
such thing as "the tenant of an ad" without the join.**

Per [`ADR-056`](../../../gks/phase2_atomic/ADR-056--shared-db-multi-tenant.md), models without
`tenantId` are skipped by the Prisma `$extends` guard, which reads the column set from DMMF.
The entire ad hierarchy sits outside that safety net by construction.

---

## 2. Decision — `firstTouchAdId` holds the Meta `ad_id`

**`Conversation.firstTouchAdId` stores `Ad.adId` (the Meta ad id), never `Ad.id` (the internal uuid).**

Three independent reasons, none of which depend on inspecting production data:

1. **Consistency.** Every other hop in the chain already joins on Meta keys. A single hop
   joining on internal uuid would make the chain unwalkable in one SQL join and would be the
   only place in the ad model where the two id spaces mix.
2. **Availability at write time.** The value arrives from Meta in a webhook, as
   `referral.ad_id`. The internal `Ad.id` may not exist yet — the ad sync worker runs on a
   schedule, so a click can reach us before the `Ad` row does. Storing the Meta id lets the
   webhook record attribution immediately; storing a uuid would require a synchronous lookup
   that can fail. See §3.
3. **Stability.** `Ad.id` is `@default(uuid())`, generated locally. If ads are ever re-synced
   into a fresh table, internal ids change and every historical attribution silently
   re-points or dangles. Meta ids are stable for the life of the ad.

The value is an opaque **numeric string** (Meta ids are numeric), which is what
`ProfileTab.jsx` already assumes when it renders the field in a monospace font.

---

## 3. Decision — no foreign key

`Conversation.firstTouchAdId` **stays a logical reference**. No `@relation`, no FK. This is the
only reference in the CRM aggregate that Phase 2 deliberately left unenforced.

**Because a FK here would drop attribution data rather than protect it.** The webhook writes a
conversation the moment a customer messages after clicking an ad. The `Ad` row is created by a
separate scheduled sync worker. Between the click and the next sync, the referenced ad does not
exist locally — and a foreign key would reject that insert. The failure mode is not "bad
attribution stored"; it is **the conversation and its messages failing to persist at all**,
on the highest-value traffic the system sees.

Secondary reasons:

- **It buys no tenant isolation.** A FK constrains one column to one parent column. It cannot
  express "and both rows belong to the same tenant", and here the parent (`Ad`) has no tenant
  to compare against (§1.1).
- **It would make ad deletion destructive.** Meta ads get archived and disappear from sync. A
  FK would force either `SetNull` (silently erasing historical attribution — the exact thing
  the immutability rule in §7 forbids) or `Restrict` (blocking ad cleanup forever).

What replaces the FK: the invariant checks in §6, run on a schedule rather than at write time.
This is a real trade — a scheduled check detects violations late instead of preventing them —
and it is the correct trade only because the alternative loses inbound messages.

---

## 4. The write path that does not exist yet

`src/app/api/webhooks/facebook/route.js` is where FEAT09 says attribution is captured. It
currently cannot capture it, for two compounding reasons:

```js
// route.js:102
if (!event.message || event.message.is_echo) continue
```

Meta delivers an ad click as a **`referral` event** (`event.referral.ad_id`), or as
`event.postback.referral` when the entry point is a button. Neither carries `event.message`, so
this line `continue`s past every event that could ever contain attribution. Even for a normal
message the field `event.message.referral` is never read.

And the conversation is created without the field:

```js
// route.js:117
const conversation = await upsertConversation(tenantId, conversationId, {
  channel: 'facebook', participantId: psid, customerId: customer.id, status: 'open',
})
```

The polling worker `src/app/api/workers/sync-messages/route.js` cannot fill the gap either: it
reads `me/conversations` with `fields: 'id,updated_time,senders...'`, and the Graph
conversations edge carries no referral data at all. Attribution is only ever available on the
live webhook event.

### 4.1 Contract for the writer

When the writer is built it must satisfy:

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| W1 | Read the ad id from `event.referral.ad_id`, `event.postback.referral.ad_id`, or `event.message.referral.ad_id`, in that order of preference. |
| W2 | Store it verbatim as the Meta id. Do **not** resolve it to `Ad.id` (§2). |
| W3 | Write it **only when creating** the conversation, or when updating a conversation whose `firstTouchAdId` is currently `NULL`. Never overwrite a non-null value (§7). |
| W4 | A referral event with no message must still create/attribute the conversation — it is the click, and it may arrive before any message. |
| W5 | Never call the Meta API from the webhook path. FEAT09 NFR3 caps webhook response at 200 ms; the ad id is already in the payload. |
| W6 | An unknown ad id is stored anyway. Attribution is a record of what Meta reported, not a claim that the ad exists locally; §6 I1 reports the divergence. |

---

## 5. As-built gaps

Everything below is verified against the code, not inferred.

| # | Gap | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| G1 | **No writer exists.** `firstTouchAdId` is never assigned anywhere in `src/`. | 4 occurrences, all reads |
| G2 | **The webhook skips referral events.** | `webhooks/facebook/route.js:102` |
| G3 | **The UI reads it off the wrong model.** `customer.firstTouchAdId` — the field is on `Conversation`. Renders "Direct" for every customer. | `ProfileTab.jsx:97,100` |
| G4 | **The tracking-health query references two non-existent columns.** `SUM(total)` — `orders` has `total_amount`; and `metadata->>'firstTouchAdId'` — `orders` has no `metadata` column at all. | `marketingRepo.js:690-691` |
| G5 | **`Customer.originId` is a second, dead attribution field.** Documented in `full-schema.md:145` as the webhook referral id; never read anywhere in `src/`. | see §8 |
| G6 | **`ADR-039` does not exist.** Two documents cite it as the authority for attribution immutability. It is absent from `gks/phase2_atomic/` and from `atomic_index.jsonl`. | `full-schema.md:207`, `data-flows/marketing.md:186` |

G3 and G4 are being repaired under a separate task and are **not** fixed here. G4 matters for
this document because it means the "unattributed revenue" number the marketing dashboard
reports has never been computed — §6 I5 gives the query that actually works.

### 5.1 Consequence for ROAS

FEAT09 defines attributable revenue as orders whose conversation has a non-null
`firstTouchAdId`. Given G1, that set is **empty**, and has always been. Every ROAS figure the
system can currently produce is either zero or derived from the failing query in G4. The note
in `FEAT15-MARKETING-AI.md:172` — "revenue มากกว่า 60% ไม่มี `firstTouchAdId`" — describes a
tracking problem, but the real figure is 100%, and the cause is that the field is never written.

---

## 6. Enforcement — invariants, since there is no FK

Full queries in [`crm-attribution-invariants.sql`](./crm-attribution-invariants.sql).

| # | Invariant | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| **I1** | Every non-null `firstTouchAdId` matches some `ads.ad_id`. | The FK's job, checked on a schedule instead of at write time (§3). A non-zero count is expected and benign shortly after a click — the ad syncs later. A count that stays non-zero means the sync worker is failing. |
| **I2** | No `firstTouchAdId` looks like a uuid. | Catches a writer that resolved to `Ad.id` in violation of §2. Meta ids are numeric strings; a 36-char hyphenated value is the wrong representation, and this is the check that makes §2 enforceable rather than aspirational. |
| **I3** | The conversation's tenant equals the tenant reached by walking `Ad → AdSet → Campaign → AdAccount`. | **This is the tenant validation #113 Phase 3 asks for.** It is impossible as a foreign key (§1.1) but perfectly possible as a query. A non-zero count means one tenant's conversation is attributed to another tenant's ad spend — a billing and isolation problem, not a data-quality one. |
| **I4** | No attributed ad has a null `ad_set_id`. | Such an ad has no path to any tenant, so I3 cannot evaluate it. These rows are a blind spot and must be reported separately rather than counted as passing. |
| **I5** | Attribution coverage and unattributed revenue, computed over the real column names. | Replaces the query in G4. Reports `orders_with_no_conversation` separately — a POS walk-in has no conversation and can never be attributed, so it is a ceiling on coverage, not a tracking failure. |
| **I6** | What `Customer.originId` actually holds, and whether any of it is recoverable. | Answers A2 before the column is dropped (§8). |

I1–I4 are the substitute for the foreign key. They should run on a schedule and alert on I2 and
I3 specifically: I1 and I4 have benign steady-state values, I2 and I3 do not.

---

## 7. Immutability

`firstTouchAdId` is **first**-touch: written once, never changed. A returning customer who
clicks a second ad does not re-attribute the original conversation.

This rule is already documented in three places — `PRD.md:206`,
`docs/gotchas/marketing-attribution.md` (G-MKT-03), `.claude/skills/domain-marketing.md:31` —
and all of them trace authority to **ADR-039, which does not exist** (G6).

Until that is resolved, this section plus rule W3 in §4.1 are the operative statement of the
rule. The proposal accompanying this document (ADR-087) records it as a decision with a real
home, so the citation chain stops dangling.

Note the interaction with §3: `onDelete: SetNull` on a `Conversation → Ad` foreign key would
*silently violate this rule* every time Meta archives an ad. Immutability is a second,
independent reason not to add the FK.

---

## 8. `Customer.originId` — retire

`Customer.originId` is documented in `full-schema.md:145` as "firstTouchAdId จาก webhook
referral" and is **never read anywhere in `src/`**. It is a second attribution field competing
with `Conversation.firstTouchAdId` for the same meaning.

Attribution belongs on `Conversation`, not `Customer`, because a customer can arrive through
several conversations from different ads; collapsing that to one field on `Customer` loses
information and makes "first touch" ambiguous — first per customer, or per conversation?

**Decision: `Conversation.firstTouchAdId` is canonical. `Customer.originId` is deprecated.**

Removal is deferred, not done: dropping a column is destructive, it needs the same audit gate
as everything else in this issue ([ADR-086 D-B](./crm-customer-360.md#8-open-decisions)), and
the column may hold values from before Phase 26 that nobody has looked at. §6 I6 counts what is
in it first. Until it is dropped it must not be read or written.

---

## 9. Open

| # | Question |
|---|---|
| A1 | Who builds the writer in §4.1, and is it in scope for FEAT-004 (Inbox) or FEAT09 (Marketing)? MOD ownership is the same gap that left the Pusher auth endpoint unbuilt. |
| A2 | Does `Customer.originId` hold anything worth migrating to `Conversation.firstTouchAdId` before it is dropped? §6 I6 answers this. |
| A3 | LINE has no equivalent of Meta's referral payload. Is first-touch attribution Facebook-only by design, or does LINE need its own mechanism? Nothing in the schema distinguishes them — `firstTouchAdId` is channel-agnostic in name but Meta-specific in content. |
